# 1 Samuel Chapter 21 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 163r–163v | **Source Image:** 1SA_021_page_001.jpg, 1SA_021_page_002.jpg

---

**1** And David came to Nob, to Ahimelech the priest. And Ahimelech came trembling to meet David and said to him, "Why are you alone, and no one is with you?"

**2** And David said to Ahimelech the priest, "The king has charged me with a matter and said to me, 'Let no one know anything of the matter about which I am sending you, and with which I have charged you.' And the young men I have directed to such and such a place.

**3** Now then, what is under your hand? Give me five loaves of bread, or whatever may be found."

**4** And the priest answered David and said, "There is no common bread under my hand, but there is holy bread — if only the young men have kept themselves from women."

**5** And David answered the priest and said to him, "Indeed, women have been kept from us as in times past when I went out, and the vessels of the young men are holy. And it is an ordinary journey — how much more so today will it be holy in their vessels."

**6** So the priest gave him the holy bread, for there was no bread there except the bread of the Presence, which had been removed from before the LORD, in order to set hot bread in its place on the day it was taken away.

**7** Now a certain man of the servants of Saul was there that day, detained before the LORD. And his name was Doeg the Edomite, the chief of the herdsmen who belonged to Saul.

**8** And David said to Ahimelech, "Is there not here under your hand a spear or a sword? For I brought neither my sword nor my weapons with me, because the king's matter was urgent."

**9** And the priest said, "The sword of Goliath the Philistine, whom you struck down in the Valley of Elah — behold, it is wrapped in a cloth behind the ephod. If you wish to take it, take it, for there is no other except that one here." And David said, "There is none like it; give it to me."

**10** And David arose and fled that day from before Saul, and came to Achish king of Gath.

**11** And the servants of Achish said to him, "Is this not David, the king of the land? Did they not sing of him in the dances, saying, 'Saul has struck down his thousands, and David his ten thousands'?"

**12** And David took these words to heart and was very much afraid before Achish king of Gath.

**13** And he changed his behavior before their eyes and feigned madness in their hands. He scratched marks on the doors of the gate and let his saliva run down upon his beard.

**14** And Achish said to his servants, "Behold, you see the man is mad. Why do you bring him to me?

**15** Am I lacking madmen, that you have brought this one to rave in my presence? Shall this one come into my house?"

**16** And David departed from there and escaped to the cave of Adullam. And when his brothers and all the house of his father heard of it, they went down to him there.

---
## SOPHIA's Council Notes
All three translators agree substantially on the narrative arc and most verse renderings. Verses 1, 3, 7, 9, 10, 12, and 16 show strong convergence across all three translations, differing only in minor stylistic choices (e.g., conjunctions, word order). The key theological terms — "bread of the Presence," "detained before the LORD," "Doeg the Edomite" — are consistent across all three. The narrative of David's deception at Nob and flight to Gath is rendered with high agreement.

---
## Disagreement Log

**Verse 1** — EMET: "And-trembled Ahimelech to-meet David"; LOGOS: "Ahimelech came trembling to meet David"; PNEUMA: "Ahimelech came trembling to meet him." SOPHIA follows LOGOS, preserving David's name for clarity.

**Verse 2** — EMET: "The-king commanded-me a-matter"; LOGOS/PNEUMA: "The king has charged me with a matter" / "The king has sent me on a mission." SOPHIA adopts LOGOS's "charged me with a matter" as the best formal rendering of the Hebrew *tsivvah*.

**Verse 4** — EMET: "common [chol] bread"; LOGOS: "common bread"; PNEUMA: "ordinary bread." SOPHIA follows EMET/LOGOS with "common bread" as the more traditional rendering of *chol*. PNEUMA's "consecrated bread" for *qodesh* versus EMET/LOGOS's "holy bread" — SOPHIA retains "holy bread" as more formally equivalent.

**Verse 5** — EMET: "vessels of-the-young-men [were]-holy"; LOGOS: "vessels of the young men are holy"; PNEUMA: "The men's bodies are ritually clean." PNEUMA interprets *kelim* ("vessels") as "bodies," which is a valid dynamic reading but loses the Hebrew metaphor. SOPHIA retains the formal "vessels of the young men" with EMET/LOGOS. Additionally, EMET: "a-common way"; LOGOS: "an ordinary journey"; PNEUMA: "ordinary missions." SOPHIA adopts LOGOS's "an ordinary journey."

**Verse 6** — EMET: "to-set hot bread on-[the]-day of-its-being-taken"; LOGOS: "in order to put hot bread in its place on the day it was taken away"; PNEUMA: "replaced with warm bread on the day it was taken away." SOPHIA follows LOGOS for clarity. PNEUMA's "warm" versus EMET/LOGOS's "hot" for *chom* — SOPHIA retains "hot."

**Verse 7** — EMET: "chief of-the-herdsmen"; LOGOS: "chief of the herdsmen"; PNEUMA: "chief of Saul's shepherds." SOPHIA follows EMET/LOGOS with "herdsmen" as more precise for *ro'im* in this context.

**Verse 8** — EMET: "both my-sword and-also my-weapons I-did-not take in-my-hand"; LOGOS: "I brought neither my sword nor my weapons with me"; PNEUMA: "I didn't bring my sword or any other weapon." SOPHIA follows LOGOS for natural English while preserving both nouns.

**Verse 11** — EMET: "Did-not of-this-one they-sing in-the-dances"; LOGOS: "Did they not sing to one another of him in the dances"; PNEUMA: "Isn't this the one they sing about in their dances." SOPHIA simplifies to "Did they not sing of him in the dances" — keeping the formal question structure from EMET/LOGOS while streamlining.

**Verse 13** — EMET: "he-changed his-discernment [ta'am]"; LOGOS: "he changed his behavior"; PNEUMA: "he changed his behavior." SOPHIA follows LOGOS/PNEUMA with "behavior" as the contextually appropriate English rendering of *ta'am*. EMET: "acted-madly [va-yitholel]"; LOGOS: "feigned madness"; PNEUMA: "pretended to be insane." SOPHIA follows LOGOS's "feigned madness" as the best balance. EMET: "let-his-spittle-run-down"; LOGOS/PNEUMA: "let his saliva run down." SOPHIA adopts "saliva" as more natural modern English.

**Verse 14** — EMET: "Behold, you-see a-man acting-madly"; LOGOS: "Behold, you see the man is mad"; PNEUMA: "Look at the man — he's out of his mind!" SOPHIA follows LOGOS, retaining "Behold" from the formal tradition.

**Verse 15** — EMET: "to-act-madly upon-me"; LOGOS: "to rave in my presence"; PNEUMA: "to carry on like a lunatic in my presence." SOPHIA follows LOGOS's "to rave in my presence" as precise and dignified.
